result.topic_en: Euler gives a numerical series for the moon's true hourly motion, corrects its constant term by comparison with the tables, and states the hourly motion in conjunction and opposition, at apogee and perigee, for lunar eclipses.

items.quote:
Haec autem formula adhuc quapiam correctione indiget, cum valor litterae $\alpha$, ob plures
[pa]rticulas ex denominatore ad eum accedentes, non satis sit certus.
items.english: This formula still needs some correction, since the value of the letter alpha is not certain enough, because several small parts from the denominator enter into it.

items.quote:
Ad hanc ergo correctionem
[inv]eniendam, calculo quaesivi duo loca lunae ad duo momenta horae intervallo differentia.
items.english: To find this correction, I computed two places of the moon at two moments differing by an interval of one hour.

items.quote:
[ubi] quidem terminum $N$ omisi, quoniam supra jam est monitum hunc terminum in excentricitate
[co]mprehendi posse.
items.english: Here I have omitted the term N, since it was noted above that this term can be included in the eccentricity.
